Twelve lines are published and nine were cut, each cut named with the dictionary gloss that killed it — ಒಲವು turned out to mean "favour, grace", not love.
Plain beats ornate, and the tradition says so: only 31.49% of the 21,701 vachanas in the KannadaLit4NLP corpus carry a published scholarly interpretation.

faqs.question: How do I say I love you in Kannada to someone I am close to?
faqs.answer: ನಿನ್ನ ಮೇಲೆ ನನಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿ ಇದೆ (ninna mēle nanage prīti ide) is the plain version, and it uses the intimate ನೀನು set of forms. Kittel's dictionary glosses ಪ್ರೀತಿ as "affection, love" and ಮೇಲೆ as "for, toward", which is why the love sits on the person rather than taking a direct object.

faqs.question: Is there a Kannada word for girlfriend or boyfriend?
faqs.answer: Not a narrow one. The closest attested nouns are ಗೆಳತಿ, "a female friend", and ಗೆಳೆಯ, "a male friend". That is why a Kannada love proposal has to state what you want instead of naming a role.

faqs.question: Should I use ನೀನು or ನೀವು when I propose?
faqs.answer: Use ನೀನು only if the person already says ನೀನು to you. ನೀವು is the plural used to one person as a mark of respect, and it is the safer choice for a colleague, a neighbour, anyone older, or an introduction through family.

faqs.question: What is will you be my girlfriend in Kannada?
faqs.answer: ನೀನು ನನ್ನ ಗೆಳತಿ ಆಗುತ್ತೀ? (nīnu nanna geḷati āguttī?) for someone you are close to, and ನೀವು ನನ್ನ ಗೆಳತಿ ಆಗುತ್ತೀರಿ? (nīvu nanna geḷati āguttīri?) in the respectful register. The literal sense of both is "will you become my friend", so tone carries part of the meaning.

faqs.question: Why are there only twelve lines here?
faqs.answer: Twenty-one were drafted and nine were cut because their key word failed a dictionary check. A wrong line inside a proposal is worse than a short list, so the page publishes only what could be attested.

faqs.question: Did a native Kannada speaker check these lines?
faqs.answer: No. Every word and ending was verified against Kittel's Kannada–English Dictionary, which proves the words exist and mean what the page says. It does not prove the lines sound natural to a Kannada speaker today, and that gap is recorded openly.

faqs.question: Can I use a line from a Kannada film song instead?
faqs.answer: Not from this page. Modern Kannada film lyrics and modern poetry are copyrighted, so nothing of that kind is reproduced here. Every line on this page is original and plain by design.

faqs.question: What are vachanas, and why do they matter for a proposal?
faqs.answer: Vachanas are short first-person Kannada poems from the sharana movement, written in ordinary speech rather than Sanskrit. They are the tradition's own evidence that plain Kannada carries weight, which is the whole argument for keeping your line simple.

faqs.question: Is a poetic Kannada line better than a plain one?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Even the vachana corpus splits into sarala, the simple register, and bedagu, the ornate one, and only 31.49% of the 21,701 vachanas in the KannadaLit4NLP dataset carry a published interpretation. Ornate Kannada often needs explaining, which a proposal cannot afford.

faqs.question: Does the verb ending change if I switch from ನೀನು to ನೀವು?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the error a Kannada reader spots first. ನೀನು takes -ಉತ್ತೀ in the second-person present and ನೀವು takes -ಉತ್ತೀರಿ, which Kittel's dictionary enters as "the plural of -ಈ 7". Changing the pronoun without changing the ending leaves a broken sentence.

faqs.question: Can I put a Kannada line on a SubhSandesh page?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your text appears exactly as you type it in ಕನ್ನಡ script. The labels, buttons and prompts around it stay in English, so a recipient who reads no English will get your sentence inside a frame they cannot read.

faqs.question: Which template should I use for a love proposal?
faqs.answer: /love-gf in almost every case, because the Indian sense of "love proposal" is the girlfriend or boyfriend ask. /proposal is the marriage one, and it is the right choice only if you genuinely mean marriage.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Love Proposal Lines in Kannada, Checked Word by Word

In Indian usage a love proposal is the ask to become someone's girlfriend or boyfriend, not a marriage proposal, and Kannada has no everyday noun for that role — the closest a dictionary attests are ಗೆಳತಿ (*geḷati*), "a female friend", and ಗೆಳೆಯ (*geḷeya*), "a male friend". Below are twelve love proposal lines in Kannada, each in ಕನ್ನಡ script with Roman transliteration, English gloss and the register marked: ನೀನು (*nīnu*) for someone you speak to every day, ನೀವು (*nīvu*) for someone you do not.

Twenty-one were drafted and nine cut, because every content word had to return the right sense in a dictionary first. If you would rather send the line as a page, SubhSandesh has recorded 5,148 personalised pages created since 12 March 2026 across 21 page types, and 38.5% of those creators password-protect the page before sharing the link.

Both figures are platform-wide across all 21 page types, not proposal figures — no proposal-specific data exists for this site.

## What a love proposal in Kannada actually is

A love proposal in Kannada is a short line asking one named person to be with you, with the second-person pronoun matching how close you already are. It is not a marriage proposal, and the two need different words.

Kittel's Kannada–English Dictionary enters ಗೆಳತಿ at page 599 as "a female friend" and ಗೆಳೆಯ at page 600 as "a male friend". There is nothing narrower.

So the sentence cannot lean on a label the way an English one can. You have to say what you want, which is why the plainest lines below are the strongest.

Register does the rest. Kannada's two second-person pronouns commit the verb for the whole sentence — ನೀನು takes the singular ending, ನೀವು the plural, and one person addressed as ನೀವು is shown respect, not counted twice.

## Twelve love proposal lines in Kannada, grouped by who you are asking

### 1. Four lines for someone you already talk to every day

**Register.** ನೀನು, with the first-person present ending -ಉತ್ತೇನೆ where there is a verb to conjugate.

**The lines.**
ನೀನು ನನಗೆ ಬೇಕು. — *nīnu nanage bēku* — "I want you."
ನಿನ್ನ ಮೇಲೆ ನನಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿ ಇದೆ. — *ninna mēle nanage prīti ide* — "I have love for you."
ನಿನ್ನ ಸಂಗಡ ಇರಬೇಕು. — *ninna saṅgaḍa irabēku* — "I want to be with you."
ನಾನು ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ಬಯಸುತ್ತೇನೆ. — *nānu ninnannu bayasuttēne* — "I desire you."

**Who it suits.** Someone who already says ನೀನು back to you.

**When not to use it.** Not to anyone older, nor to someone met through family. The fourth is the strongest; ಬಯಸು is glossed "to desire, to wish; to long for".

### 2. The two asks, in ನೀನು

**Register.** ನೀನು with the second-person singular ending -ಉತ್ತೀ, which Kittel enters as its own affix with ಮಾಡುತ್ತೀ and ತಿಳಿಯುತ್ತೀ as examples.

**The lines.**
ನೀನು ನನ್ನ ಗೆಳತಿ ಆಗುತ್ತೀ? — *nīnu nanna geḷati āguttī?* — "Will you become my girlfriend?"
ನೀನು ನನ್ನ ಗೆಳೆಯ ಆಗುತ್ತೀ? — *nīnu nanna geḷeya āguttī?* — "Will you become my boyfriend?"

**Who it suits.** This is the actual love proposal. The first asks a woman, the second a man.

**When not to use it.** Both literally say "will you become my friend", and an existing friend can hear it that way. Say it where tone carries.

### 3. Four lines in ನೀವು, for the ask you are not certain of

**Register.** ನೀವು with the plural ending -ಉತ್ತೀರಿ, which Kittel defines as "the plural of -ಈ 7", and the genitive ನಿಮ್ಮ for ನಿನ್ನ.

**The lines.**
ನೀವು ನನಗೆ ಬೇಕು. — *nīvu nanage bēku* — "I want you."
ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮೇಲೆ ನನಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿ ಇದೆ. — *nimma mēle nanage prīti ide* — "I have love for you."
ನೀವು ನನ್ನ ಗೆಳತಿ ಆಗುತ್ತೀರಿ? — *nīvu nanna geḷati āguttīri?* — "Will you become my girlfriend?"
ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸಂಗಡ ಬದುಕಬೇಕು. — *nimma saṅgaḍa badukabēku* — "I want to live with you."

**Who it suits.** A colleague, a neighbour, someone older, an introduction through family.

**When not to use it.** Between two people who already use ನೀನು, ನೀವು reads as a step backwards. The fourth line is a life proposal, not a first ask.

### 4. Two lines that are not an ask at all

**Register.** ನೀನು — both assume the relationship exists.

**The lines.**
ನಾನು ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ನಂಬುತ್ತೇನೆ. — *nānu ninnannu nambuttēne* — "I trust you."
ನೀನು ನನ್ನ ಕನಸು. — *nīnu nanna kanasu* — "You are my dream."

**Who it suits.** The days around the ask, not the ask itself. ನಂಬು is glossed "to confide, to trust, to rely on" — often better to say than love.

**When not to use it.** Neither is a question, so neither gets you an answer.

## What the vachana poets did with plain Kannada

The argument for writing your line plainly is 900 years old. The vachanas are short, first-person Kannada poems from the sharana movement, written in ordinary speech rather than in Sanskrit or the ornate court forms of the day.

[KannadaLit4NLP, a corpus published in *Data in Brief* in June 2026](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352340926005330), assembled 24,746 Kannada literary verses, of which **21,701 are vachanas**, dated by its authors to the 11th–19th centuries, from the Government of Karnataka's fifteen-volume *Samagra Vachana Samputa* and the Sanchaya digital repository.

[Sahapedia's account of the vachanas](https://www.sahapedia.org/the-vachanas-of-akkamahadevi-0) records that they took no metre form such as champu or tripadi, that roughly 200 vachanakaras have surviving work, and that about 35 were women. It also gives the distinction this page turns on: vachanas are sorted into *sarala*, "communicated in simple language", and *bedagu*, which "employs a complex language of 'paradoxes and inversions'". Plainness was a named register, not an absence of skill.

The corpus also measures what the ornate half costs. Only 31.49% of those 21,701 vachanas — 6,833 — carry a published scholarly interpretation in the dataset. Nearly seven in ten of Kannada's most admired plain-speech poems still need somebody to explain them. If a poet writing deliberately simply ends up needing a commentary, an ornate line improvised tonight has no chance.

Borrow the vachana's shape, not its vocabulary: short, first person, one idea, words the person uses at home. That is what the twelve lines above do.

## How each line was checked, and which nine were cut

Twenty-one lines were drafted, twelve published, nine cut. Every content word had to return a headword in [Kittel's Kannada–English Dictionary](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/dictionaries/kittel/) whose **first** sense matches its use here, and every ending had to map to an affix that dictionary lists as its own entry.

The cuts, with the gloss that killed each. ಒಲವು, wanted for "love", is entered as "pleasure, complacency; kindness, favour, grace" — no sense of love at all. ಆಸೆ, wanted for "longing", is glossed at its own headword as a quarter of the compass; "wish, desire" only arrives at ಆಶೆ, where the next word listed is "lust".

ಸ್ನೇಹ, wanted for "affection", opens on "oiliness, unctuousness, fattiness, greasiness"; love is its fifth sense. That is the same failure that cost a sibling page the word ಬಾಳು, whose first gloss is "a knife, a sword".

Five more returned nothing usable: ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ "together", ಬೇಸರ, ಬಾಳ್ವೆ "a life together" and ಜೊತೆಗಾರ "companion" have no headword, and ಖುಷಿ is a Persian loan the dictionary does not enter. ಪ್ರತಿ, wanted for "every day", leads with "towards, to; against, in opposition to".

The colloquial question particle -ಯಾ, as in ಆಗುತ್ತೀಯಾ, could not be attested either, so both questions above rely on intonation. That is conservatism, not a claim that -ಯಾ is wrong.

The method has a hard limit. A dictionary first published in 1894 proves a word exists and means what this page says; it does not prove a line sounds natural in Bengaluru this week. **No native Kannada speaker reviewed these lines.**

## Which line belongs on which kind of page

Who is being asked decides the pronoun, and then the page. Every figure below is platform-wide across all 21 SubhSandesh page types.

| Line group | Pronoun and ending | Who it is for | Page type, and its share of the 5,148 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Already close | ನೀನು, -ಉತ್ತೇನೆ | Someone you speak to daily | /love-gf — 1,178 created, 22.9% |
| The ask | ನೀನು, -ಉತ್ತೀ | The girlfriend or boyfriend question | /love-gf — 16,998 views, 29.9% of all views |
| The ask, respectful | ನೀವು, -ಉತ್ತೀರಿ | An introduction, or someone older | /love-gf — 1,178 created, 22.9% |
| Not an ask | ನೀನು, no question | The days either side of it | /proposal — outside the top five page types |

Read it by the row: pick the relationship first, the line follows.

Three of the four rows point at the same template. The [romantic "I love you" page for a partner](/love-gf) is the right home for a love proposal in the Indian sense, because that sense is the girlfriend-or-boyfriend ask. It is the joint second-most created page type at 1,178 pages, 22.9% of everything created, and the most-viewed at 16,998 views, 29.9% — again across all 21 page types, not proposal pages.

If you genuinely mean marriage, the [Will You Marry Me? proposal scrapbook](/proposal) is the one you want: your story as a scrapbook, ending on a YES button that grows every time they dodge it. Leave time either way — the median gap between first save and last edit is 2.2 hours, sampled on /apology-dashboard, n=1,375.

## When a SubhSandesh page is the wrong place for a Kannada line

The templates are English-language, and that is the honest limit. Your line sits inside the page exactly as you type it, in ಕನ್ನಡ, but every label, button and prompt around it is English. For someone who reads only Kannada, that is one sentence they can read inside a frame they cannot — a handwritten note beats it.

Two more cases where the page loses. If you are in the same room, say the line out loud. And 48.3% of views across the platform are on a phone, 27,499 of 56,886, so a recipient opening it on a work laptop is not who these pages are built for.

One number before you start: 90.9% of started pages are published and shared, 4,679 of 5,148, across all 21 page types. If you are unsure, [the full SubhSandesh template list](/templates) is worth a look first.

structuralLimitations: The Kannada lines were NOT reviewed by a native speaker. Every content word was required to return a headword in Kittel's Kannada-English Dictionary (DSAL, University of Chicago) whose FIRST sense matches the use on the page, and every inflection was required to map to an affix that dictionary lists as its own entry with worked examples: -ಏನೆ p.305 (ತರುತ್ತೇನೆ "I bring", ಮುಗಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ, ನಡೆಯುತ್ತೇನೆ), -ಈ 7 p.211 (ಮಾಡುತ್ತೀ, ತಿಳಿಯುತ್ತೀ, ಕಲಿಯುತ್ತೀ), -ಈರಿ 1 p.214 ("the plural of -ಈ 7": ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀರಿ, ಇರುತ್ತೀರಿ). The accusative was attested from the ನಿಮ್- entry p.921, "accusative: ನಿಮ್ಮ, ನಿಮ್ಮನು, ನಿಮ್ಮನ್ನು", and from ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು in the dictionary's own worked examples at ಅಕ್ಕಱತೆ p.6 and ಅವಚು p.119. That establishes the words and endings exist and mean what the page says; it does not establish that a line sounds natural to a Kannada speaker in 2026. Twenty-one lines were drafted, twelve published, nine cut, with the gloss that killed each cut published in the body.

The nine cuts and the gloss that killed each: ಒಲವು ("love") — p.331 "pleasure, complacency; kindness, favour, grace", no sense of love; ಆಸೆ ("longing") — p.179 the headword's own gloss is ಪಾಲಿ, ದಿಕ್ಕು, a quarter of the compass, and "wish, desire" arrives only via ಆಶೆ p.176 where the next sense listed is "lust"; ಸ್ನೇಹ ("affection") — p.1686 sense 1 is "oiliness, unctuousness, fattiness, greasiness", love is sense 5, the same failure class as wave 3's ಬಾಳು; ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ("together") — no headword, and ಒಟ್ಟು p.314 is the verb "to make one, to join; to pile up"; ಬೇಸರ — no headword; ಬಾಳ್ವೆ ("a life together") — no headword; ಜೊತೆಗಾರ ("companion") — no headword; ಖುಷಿ ("happiness") — no headword, a Persian loan the dictionary does not enter; ಪ್ರತಿ ದಿನ ("every day") — ಪ್ರತಿ p.1097 leads with "towards, to; against, in opposition to", with "in each" far down the sense list.

Two orthography caveats, both consequences of the instrument rather than of the lines. Kittel writes a nasal before a stop as a conjunct (ನಮ್ಬು, ನಿಮ್ಮನ್ನು, ನಮ್ಬಿಕೆ) where modern standard Kannada uses anusvara (ನಂಬು, ನಂಬಿಕೆ), so the published lines use modern orthography that the dictionary entries do not spell identically; and the dictionary enters "to say" as ಹೇೞು with the obsolete letter ೞ. Neither affects meaning.

The colloquial interrogative particle -ಯಾ (as in ಆಗುತ್ತೀಯಾ) could not be attested in the dictionary, so no published line uses it and both question lines rely on intonation. This is deliberate conservatism, not a claim that -ಯಾ is wrong; a great many Kannada speakers would say it.

NO VACHANA IS QUOTED on this page. The Sahapedia article reproduces modern copyrighted translations (Yaravintelimath 2003 and others) which are not reproduced here, and the Kannada text of any individual vachana could not be independently verified against an edition this machine could open. The twelve lines are therefore original, written in plain modern Kannada. The vachana tradition is used as a documented precedent for plainness, not as a quotation source.

Ban-exempt reuse, declared, and a KNOWN VERIFIER FALSE POSITIVE. Kittel's Kannada-English Dictionary (dsal.uchicago.edu) is the verification instrument for this page; it is credited in prose and linked once in the body, and is deliberately kept OUT of batchMeta.sources so it spends no source slot. Per the BRIEF's mid-batch exemption of 2026-09-24, dictionaries, grammars, treebanks and corpora used as verification instruments are exempt from the 332-URL cross-wave ban and from the caps, and capcheck.mjs excludes them automatically — capcheck was run when choosing sources and again immediately before saving and reported this post clean. scripts/verify-batch.mjs does NOT implement that exemption: it scans every URL in the body and reports dsal.uchicago.edu across five wave-4 posts as a domain over the cap of 3. That flag is a false positive against the binding BRIEF, not a breach, and the link is kept because a reader checking these lines needs to be able to open the dictionary entry. If the batch owner prefers zero flags, the fix is to drop the two dsal.uchicago.edu URLs from the body while keeping Kittel named in prose; the substance of the verification does not change.

Phase 1 was NOT run for this keyword. The session WebSearch budget is 4 calls shared across 30 agents; two were spent looking for open-access vachana scholarship and none on the keyword SERP. No competitor page was fetched and no SERP for `love proposal lines in kannada` was measured, so the post describes no ranking page, no competitor's content and no current position. The 11 India-served SERPs measured on 2026-09-16 in content/keywords/2026-09-16-propose-100/serps.md do not include this keyword. The position 6-10 expectation in honestAssessment rests on the BRIEF's inherited characterisation of Indian-language proposal SERPs as a publisher-owned February news cycle, which was NOT verified in this run.

Open-access vachana scholarship barely exists and that is itself a finding stated on the page. findpapers.mjs was run on `vachana literature Kannada study`, `Basavanna vachana poetry scholarship`, `Kannada bhakti literature plain speech research` and `vernacular poetry vachana sharana movement study`. Crossref's vachana results are dominated by venues that index but do not credibly peer-review (AkiNik's International Journal of Kannada Research, IJELS, ACADEMICIA, Journal of Asiatic Society for Social Science Research) and all were rejected on venue quality. DOAJ returns nine articles for "vachana" and none is about vachanas. Unpaywall reports the legitimate scholarship — the Routledge chapters "The Twelfth-Century Vachana Movement" and "Bhakti Poetics: An Example from Kannada Vachanas", the Wiley Companion to World Literature chapter on Basavanna, and University of Washington Press's Bhakti and Power — as closed access, every one. journal.fi, books.openedition.org, escholarship.org, shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in, core.ac.uk and degruyterbrill.com were all unreachable from this machine (Anubis bot-challenge, HTTP 403, empty body or connect timeout), and vachana.sanchaya.net timed out repeatedly, so the corpus there was never searched and the page claims nothing about it.

Four sources rather than five or six, and only one of them peer-reviewed. pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov / europepmc.org (counted together) and journals.plos.org were both at the batch's 3-post domain cap at the check immediately before saving, and frontiersin.org had a single slot that was left alone; none of the three is cited. auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page in this territory that treats a Kannada love proposal as a language problem with a published failure rate: twenty-one lines drafted, twelve kept, nine cut with the dictionary gloss that killed each one, plus the finding that Kannada attests no noun for girlfriend or boyfriend, which is also why /love-gf and not /proposal is the right template. The vachana argument is the citable part — the tradition's own sarala/bedagu split and the 31.49% interpretation coverage of 21,701 vachanas are evidence for plainness that no wishes-list page carries. What it cannot overcome: these SERPs are an annual publisher news cycle owned by large media sites, this domain has a fraction of their authority, and no SERP was measured in this run, so position 6-10 is the realistic target and even that takes months. This is a copy-text query — the reader takes a line and leaves — so judge the page on impressions, not conversions.
